heading: Publication

calibration.note: Same one-paper profile (14 proofs of arXiv 0708.2185); no new measurement was made for this problem. The rules are restated for a direct proof with two cited results.

length_basis_rhgrh100.note: The 120/168 limits came from one paper whose own median proof is about 48 words; against this corpus they sit between the 41st and 53rd percentile, so they are kept.

sentence_sample_rhgrh100.sample: 60 proofs of 40-400 words, one per paper, from mark7rhgrh100-20260928; two annotators (codex-18, zai-2), same instrument as the one-paper profile
sentence_sample_rhgrh100.reading: PR1 holds on 60 papers: commentary-only sentences are about 1 percent of proof words or less for both annotators, and most of zai-2's in-flight labels are sentence fragments. PR3 holds: separate side-condition sentences are rare. The one-paper lemma-application share (32-42) is high for this corpus (about 25, wide spread). Section lead is not reliably measured: the annotators disagree on whether setup sentences count (per-proof correlation 0.01). About one proof in twelve opens with a one-sentence statement of method (by induction; following a cited argument), which PR2 as worded would forbid; no pilot telling uses one.

rules.rule: No sentence may be commentary only (placement inflight or leaf-section). A reason for a step may appear only as a clause of the sentence that takes the step.
No restatement of the claim before the derivation; the proof opens with its first step.

Each cited result (exponent monotonicity on a probability space; the lower estimate of an L^n quantity by a bound on a set) is invoked in one sentence that says what it consumes; hypotheses are not checked in separate sentences unless the check is an argument the reader cannot be expected to supply. The positive measure of the level set is such an argument and is kept.
At most 168 words; aim for 120 or fewer.
Every mandatory node of the content plan is realized or merged with an honest quote; every dependency between nodes in the alignment is still visible in the prose.
rules.from: programme gate for P3 and P4

nodes.reason: PR2; the closing sentence states the limit.
The definition is used, not restated at length: one clause where the essential supremum first does work.
Upper bound in one sentence citing monotonicity and unit total measure (PR3).
The power limit is a standard fact; a clause in the sentence that uses it.
The level set with its purpose as a clause (PR1) and the positive-measure argument, which is a real check (PR3).
The bound at one natural exponent.
Extension to larger exponents by monotonicity, cited in the sentence that uses it.
Combine the two bounds into the limit.

why-level-set-strategy.reason: Answered as a purpose clause inside the sentence that defines the set; no separate sentence.

level-set-positive-measure.reason: The positive-measure argument is a derivation step, so it stays.

monotonicity-extension.reason: Citing monotonicity where the bound is extended is a derivation step, so it stays.

upper-bound-exponent-range.reason: A remark on a hypothesis the proof does not need is commentary; the sample proofs contain none.

note: Question decisions coincide with the expert-reference profile of the content plan. What differs is how the answers may be realized (PR1, PR3), the length (PR4), and that all eight nodes are accounted for.
